info.description: Pay distributions (direct deposit configuration) determine how a worker's pay is divided (e.g. 50% to savings, 25% to checking, $100 on a paycard, and the remainder in check). The Pay Distributions APIs can be used to change how a worker's pay is distributed, retrieve a single distribution or list all distributions, or to obtain API metadata.  For more information, see Direct Deposit API Guide for ADP Workforce Now
info.title: Worker Pay Distributions

effectiveDateTime is the date that the event is effective from a business perspective
/data/schemaContext communicates the keys and properties that relate the event instance to a concrete concept (e.g. associate).
The only information that must be valued in the meta for the events header are the standard codelist references for priorityCode, eventStatusCode, and serviceCategoryCode
All envelope data is set by the System of Record (e.g. event.ID, creationDateTime, recordDateTime, event.status.code, etc…

An SOR may return an HTTP 503 when they are down for a scheduled maintenance or for an outage.If an SOR is planning a maintenance window then they should plan on having an end point available to return the 503 with a standard confirmMessage.  The confirmMessage will contain a message stating the date and timeframe that the maintenance window is for.The SOR should return the Retry-After response-header field with the Date and Time when they expect the system to be available.  E.g. §  Retry-After: Fri, 31 Dec 1999 23:59:59 GMT  This does not need to be handled dynamically.  They can set the time that their maintenance window ends.
/data/output communicates the result of the event instance.
An event which is being recorded includes the /data/eventContext and the /data/transform during the composition phase (i.e. recording of the event).

/data/input is optional.  Input communicates data that is needed to complete recording the event instance.  An example is a benefits.enroll event.  The input communicates the benefitOfferings (the choices) that the user has to make which are communicated in the transform.

post.description:
The /events/payroll/v1/worker.pay-distribution.change request replaces an employee's existing Direct Deposit records with an updated array collection in the request payload. 

There are no separate/explicit Add, Update, Remove, and Inactivate URI's. For example, if a new Direct Deposit needs to be added to an existing collection, your application needs to first, retrieve the existing collection, then build the request payload with the existing collection and insert the new Direct Deposit record in the array. To delete a Direct Deposit, your application needs to remove the record from the array and send the rest of the collection in the request payload. 

The Direct Deposit API is supported for both U.S. and Canadian clients. The following are the differences between the two types of clients: 

For U.S. clients: The Routing Number and Account Number are used to add and update a Direct Deposit. 

For Canadian clients: The Bank name and Branch code, along with the Account Number, are used to add and update a Direct Deposit. 

Refer the payloads in the API Usage section. 

In the given payload (pay-distribution.change_Payload), the following is the purpose of the eventContext and transform sections: 

eventContext: A set of keys, identifying the subject. In the payload, the associateID field is present under eventContext. The associateID identifies the subject. 

transform: Provides the values added or changed with respect to the subject keys defined in the eventContext section..

get.description:
Returns Direct Deposits based on the pay-distribution-id.
Tip: When an associate has more than one position, each position has a unique payrollGroupCode and payrollFileNumber. The user can retrieve all the Direct Deposits of company codes for all positions using GET /payroll/v2/workers/{aoid}/pay-distributions.

If the user wants to retrieve Direct Deposits of only one position, the user can make use of the GET /payroll/v2/workers/{aoid} /pay-distributions/{pay-distribution-id}. The API is called by passing the {pay-distribution-id} of the particular position. The {pay-distribution-id} value is obtained from the GET /payroll/v2/workers /{aoid}/pay-distributions call.


To address privacy concerns, clients can configure if to allow a user access bank account number and routing numbers. As part of your client onboarding process, you need to make sure clients confirm security settings for your connector user security profile by following the steps in Appendix: Update the Security Profile to Retrieve Unmasked Bank Routing Numbers and Account Numbers. By default, Account Number and Routing Number are masked in the Direct Deposit API response. To reveal masked data, simply add the following header to your HTTP request:

Accept:application/json;masked=false
